map.反应距离叠加减速制动距离。: Reaction distance plus deceleration braking distance.
map.d = v₀t_r + v₀²/(2a)。 100 km/h、反应1s、减速度7: d = v₀t_r + v₀²/(2a). 100 km/h, reaction 1s, deceleration 7 → about 60 m.
map.含反应距离的全程刹停距离。: Total stopping distance including reaction distance.
map.把反应距离与制动距离相加，评估总停车距离。: Add reaction distance and braking distance to evaluate total stopping distance.
map.车速 20 m/s，反应时间 1.5 s，: Vehicle speed 20 m/s, reaction time 1.5 s,
map.反应距离=v₀·t_r=20×1.5=30.00 m；制动距离=v₀²/(2a): Reaction distance=v₀·t_r=20×1.5=30.00 m; braking distance=v₀²/(2a)=400/10=40.00 m; total stopping distance=70.00 m. At 72 km/h you need about 70 m to stop.
map.反应距离占比大吗？: Is the reaction distance a large proportion?
map.100km/h 下反应 1 秒就走 27.8 米，占全程约 1/3；疲劳/分神会: At 100km/h, reacting 1 s travels 27.8 m, about 1/3 of the total; fatigue/distraction significantly lengthens it, so keep distance.
map.为什么速度翻倍时制动距离变四倍？: Why does braking distance become four times when speed doubles?
map.制动距离=v₀²/(2a)，与速度平方成正比。速度从 20 变到 40 m/s: Braking distance=v₀²/(2a), proportional to the square of speed. When speed goes from 20 to 40 m/s, the braking segment grows from 40.00 m to 160.00 m. This is also the fundamental reason high-speed driving must greatly increase following distance — danger does not grow linearly.
